title: Profit on paper, empty bank
principle: Businesses die when cash runs out, not when profit does.

screens.text: Jet Airways once flew more than 120 planes. On 17 April 2019 it ran its last flight, with no cash left for fuel.

screens.prompt: What can stop a big airline in a single day?

options.label: Its customers all leave at once
It can't pay this week's bills

screens.why: Banks said no to ₹400 crore of emergency money. Without it, Jet couldn't pay for fuel. Pilots had gone four months without pay.

screens.title: Three different numbers
screens.text: Sales are all the money that comes in. Profit is what's left after costs. Cash is what you hold today. Only cash pays bills.

screens.title: Sunil's uniforms
screens.text: Sunil sews school uniforms. Each week he spends ₹30,000 and bills ₹45,000, so he makes ₹15,000 profit. But the school chain pays after 90 days.

screens.prompt: Sunil starts with ₹1,20,000 in the bank. In which week does it run out?

options.label: Week 13, when the first payment is due
Never. He makes ₹15,000 profit a week

screens.why: ₹1,20,000 ÷ ₹30,000 = 4 weeks of bills. The first payment comes after 90 days, about week 13. He is empty from week 5.

wrong.a: Week 13 is when money starts coming in. His bills start in week 1.
wrong.b: The profit is real, but it's on paper. The cash leaves every week and comes back 90 days later.

screens.prompt: To keep paying until the school pays in week 13, how much more cash does Sunil need?
screens.why: 13 weeks × ₹30,000 = ₹3,90,000 of bills. He has ₹1,20,000, so he is ₹2,70,000 short. And his books say he is 'making' ₹15,000 a week.

wrong.b: That's all 13 weeks of bills. He already has ₹1,20,000 of it.
wrong.c: That's one week's billing. He needs to cover 13 weeks of costs first.

options.label: Take on a second school chain

screens.why: At 30 days, money starts coming in around week 5, so his ₹1,20,000 nearly covers the wait. A higher price changes the profit, not the timing.

wrong.a: More profit, but it still arrives in week 13. He's still empty in week 5.
wrong.c: A second chain doubles his weekly bills while he waits. He'd run dry in about half the time.

screens.prompt: Sunil owes ₹20,000 in wages on Saturday. What can he pay them with?

items.text: A ₹30,000 bill the buyer pays in 60 days

screens.why: Orders, unpaid bills, stock and refunds can all be worth money. None of them pays the wages on Saturday.

screens.prompt: Pooja's gym has ₹3,00,000 in the bank. Each month ₹1,50,000 goes out and ₹1,00,000 comes in. How many months can she last?
screens.why: She loses ₹1,50,000 − ₹1,00,000 = ₹50,000 a month. ₹3,00,000 ÷ ₹50,000 = 6 months. That number is her runway. Count her own fixed wage in the ₹1,50,000, too.

wrong.a: That divides by everything going out. Money still comes in each month, so count only the gap.
wrong.b: Check the gap: ₹1,50,000 out, ₹1,00,000 in. She loses ₹50,000 a month.

screens.setup: A second school chain offers Sunil ₹90,000 of work a week. It would cost him ₹60,000 a week. It also pays after 90 days.
screens.question: That's ₹30,000 more profit a week. What do you do?

options.label: Say yes. It triples the business
options.outcome: His weekly bills jump to ₹90,000. His ₹1,20,000 is gone before week 2 ends. He can't buy cloth for either school.
options.why: Growth eats cash first and pays it back later. Bigger orders on long credit empty the bank faster.
options.better: Take it only if the money comes sooner, like an advance or 30-day terms.

options.label: Yes, with 40% up front and 30-day terms
options.outcome: The ₹36,000 advance each week pays more than half the new costs. Money starts coming back in a month, not three.
options.why: He checked when the cash comes in, as well as the profit. Same order, but now he can survive it.

options.label: Say no. It's too risky
options.outcome: Sunil stays safe, but he turns away ₹30,000 a week without asking for better terms.
options.why: Safe, but he never tried to fix the timing.
options.better: Ask for an advance and shorter terms before saying no.

screens.text: A profitable business can still shut if ___ hits zero before ___ pay.
screens.why: Profit says the business works. Only cash keeps it open. Jet had 119 planes at the end of 2018. Four months later it had no cash for fuel.

summary: Sales come in, profit is what's left, cash is what you hold today.
Long credit and fast growth can empty a profitable business.
Runway = cash ÷ the monthly gap between money out and money in.

cards.front: You make ₹20,000 profit a month, but buyers pay in 90 days. What should you watch most?
options: Cash in the bank each week
cards.back: Cash. Profit that arrives in 90 days can't pay this week's bills.

cards.front: ₹2,40,000 in the bank. You lose ₹40,000 a month. How long can you last?
A big new order pays in 90 days. What makes it safe?
cards.back: Bring the cash closer. Growth on long credit empties the bank.
